items.label: HB_ITEM_ANT
items.fact_en: A queen of this little black garden ant can live for up to 29 years.

items.label: HB_ITEM_LADYBIRD
items.fact_en: The seven-spot ladybird has three spots on each wing case and one shared in the middle.

items.label: HB_ITEM_BEE
items.fact_en: A busy hive can hold as many as 60,000 worker bees.

items.label: HB_ITEM_SNAIL
items.fact_en: A Roman snail can live for 20 years, and its shell grows along with it.

items.label: HB_ITEM_TENNIS_BALL
items.fact_en: Tennis balls turned yellow in 1972 so they would show up better on television.

items.label: HB_ITEM_FROG
items.fact_en: The edible frog is a cross between two other frogs, the pool frog and the marsh frog.

items.label: HB_ITEM_MOUSE
items.fact_en: A house mouse's tail can be as long as the rest of its body.

items.label: HB_ITEM_BUTTERFLY
items.fact_en: Monarchs fly up to 2,800 miles to spend the winter in Mexico's mountain forests.

items.label: HB_ITEM_FOOTBALL
items.fact_en: The laws of the game ask for a ball 68 to 70 cm around, which makes it this wide.

items.label: HB_ITEM_CRAB
items.fact_en: Its scientific name means 'savoury beautiful swimmer'.

items.label: HB_ITEM_CAT
items.fact_en: Cats sleep 12 to 16 hours a day.

items.label: HB_ITEM_RABBIT
items.fact_en: A rabbit's ears are 7 to 8 cm long, about a fifth of its whole body.

items.label: HB_ITEM_CHICKEN
items.fact_en: There are more than 26 billion chickens, over three for every person on Earth.

items.label: HB_ITEM_DOG
items.fact_en: A Labrador stands 55 to 57 cm at the shoulder, a good middle among big dogs.

items.label: HB_ITEM_SHEEP
items.fact_en: A sheep's slit-shaped pupils let it see behind itself without turning its head.

items.label: HB_ITEM_PENGUIN
items.fact_en: Emperor penguins dive deeper than 500 metres and stay under for 20 minutes.

items.label: HB_ITEM_COW
items.fact_en: A Holstein gives about 10,000 kg of milk a year, some 27 litres every day.

items.label: HB_ITEM_HORSE
items.fact_en: Horses are measured at the withers, and they can sleep standing up.

items.label: HB_ITEM_PERSON
items.fact_en: Around the world, men average about 171 cm tall and women about 160 cm.

items.label: HB_ITEM_BICYCLE
items.fact_en: A road bike is longer than its rider is tall.

items.label: HB_ITEM_DOOR
items.fact_en: Most house doors are 80 inches tall, so nearly everyone walks under without ducking.

items.label: HB_ITEM_ELEPHANT
items.fact_en: The African bush elephant is the largest animal walking on land.

items.label: HB_ITEM_CROCODILE
items.fact_en: The saltwater crocodile is the largest reptile alive today.

items.label: HB_ITEM_CAR
items.fact_en: A family hatchback is about as long as two and a half people lying head to toe.

items.label: HB_ITEM_SHARK
items.fact_en: A great white has about 300 serrated teeth and keeps growing new ones.

items.label: HB_ITEM_GIRAFFE
items.fact_en: A giraffe's long neck has just seven bones, the same number as yours.

items.label: HB_ITEM_ORCA
items.fact_en: A male orca's back fin stands 1.8 metres tall, higher than most people.

items.label: HB_ITEM_BUS
items.fact_en: A city bus is almost exactly as long as a T. rex.

items.label: HB_ITEM_TREX
items.fact_en: Sue, one of the most complete T. rex skeletons, is more than 12 metres long.

items.label: HB_ITEM_WHALE
items.fact_en: The blue whale is the largest animal ever known; its heart alone weighs 180 kg.
